async def call(p):
    await asyncio.sleep(1)
    return p

async def main():
    start = time.perf_counter()
    await asyncio.gather(call("a"), call("b"), call("c"))
    print(f"{time.perf_counter() - start:.0f}s")
why: gather starts all three calls together, so they wait at the same time.

c:
async def main():
    start = time.perf_counter()
    await call("a")
    await call("b")
    await call("c")
    print(f"{time.perf_counter() - start:.0f}s")
q: Same call function. What does it print now?
why: Each await finishes before the next one starts, so the waits add up.

async def call(p):
    time.sleep(1)   # not asyncio.sleep
    return p

... await asyncio.gather(call("a"), call("b"), call("c"))
q: It uses gather, so what does it print?
why: time.sleep blocks the whole event loop, so nothing else can run. Use await asyncio.sleep inside async code.

q: The await is missing. What do you see?
o: A coroutine object and a warning
why: Without await you get the unfinished job, not its result. The 0x... number differs on every run.

c:
class ChatRequest(BaseModel):
    question: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=2000)
    top_k: int = Field(default=3, ge=1, le=10)

print(ChatRequest(question="What is E101?", top_k="5"))
q: top_k is the text "5". What happens?
o: It prints top_k=5, as a number
why: Pydantic converts text that clearly means a number. Bad values are refused.

q: top_k must be between 1 and 10. What happens with 99?
o: A ValidationError that says it must be at most 10
why: Pydantic is the bouncer: bad data is stopped at the door, with a message that says why.
